content.title: About
content.content: Raw egg yolk, frozen and pasteurized, is the liquid part of the egg that has undergone heat treatment to eliminate pathogenic microorganisms. The product retains most of the nutrients found in fresh yolk and is convenient for long‑term storage.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pasteurization allows safe use of yolk in dishes that require a raw texture, such as sauces and desserts.
Freezing preserves the color and structure of the yolk, preventing separation when thawed.
Egg yolk contains almost all of the egg’s nutrients: vitamins A, D, E, K, as well as biotin, folate, and minerals.
Pasteurized yolk is widely used in the food industry for making mayonnaise, dressings, and confectionery products.
When stored properly at –18 °C, the product remains stable for up to 12 months.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Vitamin A supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin D
items.content: Vitamin D aids calcium absorption and promotes bone health.

items.title: Contains choline
items.content: Choline is essential for brain function, liver health, and fat metabolism.

items.title: High in lecithin
items.content: Lecithin improves emulsification, making yolk valuable in sauces and baked goods.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs may experience reactions, up to anaphylaxis, from consuming yolk.

items.title: High cholesterol content
items.content: Yolk contains cholesterol; people with elevated cholesterol should consume it in moderation.

items.title: Proper thawing required
items.content: Improper thawing can allow bacterial growth; always thaw in the refrigerator.

items.title: Observe storage times
items.content: After thawing, use the yolk within 2–3 days and keep it refrigerated.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Pasteurized frozen yolk is suitable for making mayonnaise, sauces, custards, baked goods, desserts, and protein shakes. Thaw in the fridge, then whisk until smooth.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen yolk at –18 °C in an airtight package. Once thawed, store in the refrigerator for no more than 2–3 days and use within that period.
